corrections.corrected_statement: A first time Nevada driver license issued to a person under age sixty five is valid for eight years and expires on the birthday unless limited term immigration documents are presented, in which case expiration follows the verified departure date or one year if none is provided.
corrections.note: Added the limited term immigration document exception that the original omitted.

corrections.corrected_statement: A first time license for a person under age sixty five is valid for eight years unless limited term immigration documents apply, a license for a person age sixty five or older is valid for four years, and an identification card is valid for eight years.
corrections.note: Added the limited term immigration document exception missing from the summary.

corrections.corrected_statement: Do not leave a child aged seven or younger alone in a vehicle when conditions create a significant risk to health and safety unless a person at least twelve years old supervises the child and keeps the child in sight.
corrections.note: Added the missing limiting condition about significant risk to health and safety.

corrections.corrected_statement: White lines may separate same direction traffic but are also used to mark highway edges and shoulders and crosswalks and stop lines while yellow lines separate opposite direction traffic.
corrections.note: Removed always because white lines have other uses besides separating same direction traffic.

corrections.corrected_statement: Three different six-month rules apply to Nevada teens: hold the permit at least six months, carry no non-family passengers under 18 for the first six months of licensed driving, and stay crash- and conviction-free for six months before licensing.
corrections.note: The crash-free rule is stated on page 14, not on the cited page 15.
